## Database tables impacted by an `editrecipe.aspx` change

Tracing the full round trip ΓÇö page load, category dropdown, image handling, the save/update action, plus the shared master page and side controls (`sidemenu`, `newestarticle`, `searchtab`, `Login.ascx`) that render alongside it ΓÇö **12 distinct tables** are touched:

| # | Table | Access | Why it's touched |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | `dbo.Recipes` | **read/write** | Core of the page: load recipe for editing, and `spUpdateRecipe` saves the changes |
| 2 | `dbo.usersmain` (Users) | read/write | Login/auth checks (`spVerifyUserLoginCredential`, `spGetUserID`); `spSelectUser` also bumps a `Hits` counter when the side menu resolves the user's role |
| 3 | `dbo.RECIPE_CAT` | read | Populates the recipe-category dropdown (used both on the edit form and the search tab) |
| 4 | `dbo.RecipeUpdateLog` | write | Audit row inserted by `spUpdateRecipe` on every successful save |
| 5 | `dbo.ExceptionLog` | write | Written only if `BasePage.Page_Error` catches an unhandled exception |
| 6 | `dbo.PrivateMessage` | read | New-message count shown in the header login box (every page via the master) |
| 7 | `dbo.FriendsList` | read | Unapproved-friend-request count in the header login box |
| 8 | `dbo.Cooking_Article` | read | "Newest articles" side panel; also counted inside `spSelectUser` |
| 9 | `dbo.Cooking_Article_Category` | read | Joined by the newest-articles panel query |
| 10 | `dbo.userCookBook` | read | Saved-recipe count inside `spSelectUser` |
| 11 | `dbo.COMMENTS_RECIPE` | read | Comment count inside `spSelectUser` |
| 12 | `dbo.COMMENTS_ARTICLE` | read | Comment count inside `spSelectUser` |

**Of these, only `Recipes` and `RecipeUpdateLog` are directly tied to the edit action itself** ΓÇö the other 10 come from shared chrome (master page login box, side menu, article panel, search tab) that renders on every request to this page, so a change to the page's layout/controls could pull those in too, while a change scoped purely to the save logic mainly concerns `Recipes`, `RecipeUpdateLog`, and incidentally `RECIPE_CAT` (category name lookup) and `usersmain` (ownership check).

One thing worth flagging: `RecipeDetails.FillUp` (the "load recipe for edit" call) passes a literal SQL string into `DataAccess.GetFromReader`, which always executes as `CommandType.StoredProcedure` ΓÇö this looks like broken/leftover code (a commented-out call to the real `spGetRecipeDetail` proc sits right above it) and would likely fail at runtime rather than run as inline SQL. Worth checking if you touch that path.

## Database tables impacted by the `editrecipe.aspx` flow

Tracing both entry points in the code-behind ΓÇö `Page_Load` (loads the recipe for editing) and `Update_Recipe` (saves changes) ΓÇö through every BLL/provider call down to the stored procedures in `App_Data/XDPortal.sql`, **4 tables are directly impacted**, plus 1 table touched only on the error-handling path.

| # | Table | How it's touched | Triggered by |
|---|-------|-------------------|--------------|
| 1 | **`dbo.Recipes`** | `SELECT` (raw SQL) to fetch the recipe being edited; `SELECT` (`GetRecipeImageFileNameForUpdate`) to get the current image; `UPDATE` (`spUpdateRecipe`) writes Name, CAT_ID, Category, Ingredients, Instructions, HITS, RecipeImage, UID; also read in a `COUNT(*)` subquery used by the category dropdown proc | `Page_Load` ΓåÆ `RecipeDetails.FillUp` / `GetRecipeImage.GetRecipeImageUserEdit`; `Update_Recipe` ΓåÆ `RecipeRepository.Update` ΓåÆ `spUpdateRecipe` |
| 2 | **`dbo.RECIPE_CAT`** | `SELECT` (`spSelectRecipeCategory`) populates the Category dropdown; `SELECT` inside `spUpdateRecipe` to resolve `CAT_TYPE` when the category changes | `Page_Load` ΓåÆ `LoadDropDownListCategory.LoadDropDownCategory`; `Update_Recipe` ΓåÆ `spUpdateRecipe` |
| 3 | **`dbo.RecipeUpdateLog`** | `INSERT` (RID, UID, DateUpdated) logged on every successful update | `Update_Recipe` ΓåÆ `spUpdateRecipe` |
| 4 | **`dbo.usersmain`** | `SELECT` (`spGetUserID`) resolves the logged-in user's ID for the ownership check and to stamp `UID`; `SELECT` (`spVerifyUserLoginCredential`) gates the whole page via `IsUserAuthenticated`; `SELECT` (`spSelectUserStatus`) checks for a suspended account | `UserIdentity.UserID`, `Authentication.IsUserAuthenticated` ΓÇö called at the top of `Page_Load` and again in `Update_Recipe` |
| 5 | **`dbo.ExceptionLog`** *(indirect)* | `INSERT` via `spInsertExceptionError`, only fires if an unhandled exception escapes the page | `BasePage.Page_Error`, inherited by `editrecipe` |

**Not database-backed:** the recipe photo itself is saved to the filesystem (`RecipeImageUpload/` folder) by `ImageUploadManager.UploadRecipeImage` ΓÇö only the resulting filename string lands in `Recipes.RecipeImage`. The ASP.NET cache purge calls (`Caching.PurgeCacheItems`) are in-memory only, not DB.

**So: 4 tables are directly in the recipe-edit data path, 5 if you count the shared exception-logging path.**

One thing worth flagging while I was in there: `ProviderRecipeDetail.cs:136` (`GetRecipeDetail`) uses a hand-built SQL string instead of the `spGetRecipeDetail` stored procedure (which still exists, just commented out), and has a logic bug ΓÇö the fallback branch checks `@prmApproved IS NULL AND ID = @prmApproved` instead of `ID = @prmID`, so it can never actually match. Parameters are still passed via `SqlParameter`, so it isn't SQL-injectable, but if your change touches recipe retrieval you'll likely want to fix or at least be aware of this.

Confirmed ΓÇö `Recipes` is fully denormalized (Category name, ratings, comment counts all live as columns on the table itself, not via joins). That closes out the analysis.

## Summary: `editrecipe.aspx` end-to-end DB impact

Tracing the flow: `Page_Load` ΓåÆ `RecipeDetails.FillUp` / `GetRecipeImage.GetRecipeImageUserEdit` / `LoadDropDownListCategory` (populate form), and `Update_Recipe` ΓåÆ `RecipeRepository.Update` ΓåÆ `ActionProcedureDataProvider` ΓåÆ stored procs ΓåÆ tables.

**5 tables can be impacted:**

| # | Table | How it's touched | Where |
|---|-------|-------------------|-------|
| 1 | **`dbo.Recipes`** | Read (recipe detail, current image) and **Write** (name, category, ingredients, instructions, hits, image, UID updated) | `GetRecipeDetail` (inline SQL), `GetRecipeImageFileNameForUpdate`, `spUpdateRecipe` |
| 2 | **`dbo.RECIPE_CAT`** | Read ΓÇö populates the category dropdown, and looked up again server-side to denormalize the category name onto the Recipes row | `spSelectRecipeCategory`, and inside `spUpdateRecipe` (`SELECT @CatName = CAT_TYPE FROM RECIPE_CAT`) |
| 3 | **`dbo.RecipeUpdateLog`** | **Write** ΓÇö an audit row (`RID`, `UID`, `DateUpdated`) is inserted on every successful update | `spUpdateRecipe` (`INSERT INTO dbo.RecipeUpdateLog...`) |
| 4 | **`dbo.usersmain`** | Read ΓÇö authenticates the current user and resolves their `UID` (used to gate access and to stamp `UID` on the recipe update) | `spGetUserID`, `spVerifyUserLoginCredential`, `spSelectUserStatus`, called via `Authentication.IsUserAuthenticated` / `UserIdentity.UserID` |
| 5 | **`dbo.ExceptionLog`** | **Write** (conditional ΓÇö only on an unhandled exception on the page) | `BasePage.Page_Error` ΓåÆ `spInsertExceptionError` |

Notes for planning your change:
- `Recipes` is fully denormalized ΓÇö `Category`, `RATING`, `NO_RATES`, `TOTAL_COMMENTS`, `HIT_DATE` are columns on the row itself, not joined from other tables, so a recipe-detail query only ever touches this one table plus `RECIPE_CAT` for the category name.
- Cache purging (`Caching.PurgeCacheItems("MainCourse_RecipeCategory")`, etc.) happens on update but is in-memory only, not DB.
- If your change adds new fields or alters validation/business rules, tables 1ΓÇô3 are the ones you'll actually be modifying logic against; 4 and 5 are cross-cutting infrastructure the page depends on but likely won't need changes unless you're touching auth or error handling.

## Flow traced

| Step | Code path | DB call |
|---|---|---|
| Page load ΓÇö auth check | `Authentication.IsUserAuthenticated` ΓåÆ `UserIdentity.UserID` ΓåÆ `Blogic.GetUserID` / `Blogic.UserLoginVerify` / `Blogic.IsUserActive` | `spGetUserID`, `spVerifyUserLoginCredential`, `spSelectUserStatus` |
| Page load ΓÇö category dropdown | `LoadDropDownListCategory.LoadDropDownCategory` ΓåÆ `ProviderRecipeCategoryDropdown` ΓåÆ `Blogic.GetRecipeCategoryDropdownlist` | `spSelectRecipeCategory` |
| Page load ΓÇö recipe image | `GetRecipeImage.GetRecipeImageUserEdit` ΓåÆ `Blogic.GetRecipeImageFileNameForUpdate` | `GetRecipeImageFileNameForUpdate` |
| Page load ΓÇö recipe detail | `RecipeDetails.FillUp` ΓåÆ `Blogic.GetRecipeDetail` (inline SQL) | `SELECT * FROM Recipes` |
| Submit ΓÇö image fallback | `ImageUploadManager.UploadRecipeImage` ΓåÆ `Blogic.GetRecipeImageFileNameForUpdate` (when no new file uploaded) | `GetRecipeImageFileNameForUpdate` |
| Submit ΓÇö save | `RecipeRepository.Update` ΓåÆ `Blogic.UpdateRecipe` | `spUpdateRecipe` |

`spUpdateRecipe` itself does three things: verifies ownership against `Recipes`, updates `Recipes` (and looks up the category name from `RECIPE_CAT` when the category changed), and inserts an audit row into `RecipeUpdateLog`. `Caching.PurgeCacheItems` calls are in-memory ASP.NET cache invalidation ΓÇö no DB impact.

## Result: 4 tables impacted

1. **`Recipes`** ΓÇö read (detail load, image lookup, ownership check) and written (the update itself)
2. **`RECIPE_CAT`** ΓÇö read (category dropdown list, and category-name lookup inside `spUpdateRecipe`)
3. **`RecipeUpdateLog`** ΓÇö written (audit-log insert on every successful update)
4. **`usersmain`** ΓÇö read (authentication/identity checks that gate page load and the update action)

If your planned change touches only the recipe fields (name/ingredients/instructions/category/image), `Recipes`, `RECIPE_CAT`, and `RecipeUpdateLog` are the ones at risk; `usersmain` is only relevant if you touch the auth/ownership logic.

I traced `editrecipe.aspx` ΓåÆ `editrecipe.aspx.cs` ΓåÆ the BLL provider classes it calls ΓåÆ the DAL (`ActionStoredPrecedure.cs`) ΓåÆ the actual stored procedures/inline SQL in `App_Data/XDPortal.sql`. Here's the full picture, split into what the edit-recipe logic itself touches vs. what's touched only because of shared page chrome rendered around it.

## Core tables ΓÇö directly used by the edit-recipe flow (3)

| # | Table | How it's touched | Where |
|---|-------|-------------------|-------|
| 1 | **`Recipes`** | Read on `Page_Load` (`GetRecipeDetail`, `GetRecipeImageFileNameForUpdate`), **write** on submit (`spUpdateRecipe` does the `UPDATE`) | `editrecipe.aspx.cs`, `RecipeDetails.FillUp`, `GetRecipeImage`, `RecipeRepository.Update` |
| 2 | **`RECIPE_CAT`** | Read ΓÇö populates the category dropdown (`spSelectRecipeCategory`) and looked up for the category-name denormalized column during update (`spUpdateRecipe` reads `CAT_TYPE`) | `LoadDropDownListCategory` ΓåÆ `ProviderRecipeCategoryDropdown`; `spUpdateRecipe` |
| 3 | **`usersmain`** | Read ΓÇö gates the whole page (`Authentication.IsUserAuthenticated`, ownership check `Recipe.UID == UserIdentity.UserID`) via `spVerifyUserLoginCredential` / `spSelectUserStatus` | `Authentication.cs` |

This is the tight blast radius: if you're modifying the *actual* add/edit-recipe logic (fields, validation, image handling, category assignment, ownership check), these 3 are what you need to worry about.

## Incidental tables ΓÇö touched because of shared page chrome (4)

`editrecipe.aspx` uses `SiteTemplate2.master` (which embeds the `Login.ascx` control) and its own `LeftPanel` includes `sidemenu.ascx`, `newestarticle.ascx`, `rsssidemenu.ascx`. These run on nearly every page in the site, not because of anything specific to recipe editing:

| # | Table | How it's touched | Where |
|---|-------|-------------------|-------|
| 4 | **`PrivateMessage`** | Read ΓÇö unread-message count badge in the login box | `Login.ascx` ΓåÆ `GetUserNewPrivateMessageCount` (`spSelectUserNewPrivateMessage`) |
| 5 | **`FriendsList`** | Read ΓÇö unapproved friend-request badge in the login box | `Login.ascx` ΓåÆ `GetCountUnApprovedFriends` (`spSelectCountUnApprovedFriends`) |
| 6 | **`Cooking_Article`** | Read ΓÇö "Newest Articles" sidebar widget | `newestarticle.ascx` ΓåÆ `NewestArticleMenuProvider.GetArticle` |
| 7 | **`ExceptionLog`** | Write ΓÇö only if the page throws an unhandled exception | `BasePage.Page_Error` ΓåÆ `LogExceptionError` (`spInsertExceptionError`) |

## Total: 7 tables (3 core, 4 incidental)

If your change stays inside `editrecipe.aspx.cs` and the recipe-specific BLL/DAL path, only **`Recipes`, `RECIPE_CAT`, `usersmain`** are at risk. The other 4 only matter if your change also touches the master page, the login control, or the sidebar controls it includes.
